thread:
Alex (support): FYI customer CUST-5421 reporting intermittent 502/504s from hosted API since ~09:15 UTC. They see long tail latency spikes at p95/p99 and a bunch of timeouts. Customer pasted curl output showing 504.
Alex (support): curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' \\n  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1\",\"input\":\"short test\"}'
Alex (support): response headers: x-request-id: r-9f3b, x-hosted-error: gateway_timeout, status: 504
Priya (sre): Thanks Alex. Can you grab request_queue_depth & continuous_batch_backlog graphs for that tenant? Also any ejects/fallbacks logged?
Alex (support): Pulling metrics now, attaching screenshot (small). Looks like request_queue_depth for tenant: 1024 at peak, continuous_batch_backlog spikes to ~1400.
Priya (sre): Oof. Queue depth > configured max_queue_depth (defaults to 1000). Might be hitting early reject path or blocking dequeue. Any recent deploys? @deploy-bot were there infra rollouts ~09:00?
deploy-bot: deploy:release/2026.03.17 deployed to prod at 08:52 UTC (job id: 20260317-1145). No batcher service restarts on that release.
Dave (runtime): I can repro locally with a traffic generator. Behavior: when backlog > ~1k, continuous batcher threads start stalling on kv-cache lock and we see backpressure across gateway. Logs: 
```
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z batcher[pid=78] WARN dequeue_delay=512ms queue_depth=1058 model=redwood-1
2026-03-17T09:12:04Z runtime ERROR kvcache: lock contention wait=128ms key=token_prefix
2026-03-17T09:12:05Z gateway WARN request_timeout id=r-9f3b status=504
```
Priya (sre): That kvcache lock wait is suspicious. We saw a similar pattern last quarter but it was mitigated by adding per-tenant kvcache shards. Did the shard count for hosted env go down?
Dave (runtime): Checking config: hosted kvcache_shards=16 for prod. However, I see a hot shard: shard=3 showing 85% CPU and high contention. The batcher threads are queuing waiting for cache writes when large prefixes are being inserted.
Marta (pm): Customer impact: a single tenant burst (large batch of short requests) hitting a model with long prefix evals caused queue to pile up. They expect SLA. Do we have a short-term mitigation we can apply now?
Priya (sre): Short-term options: 1) throttle tenant at ingress (rate-limit / spike protect) 2) increase max_queue_depth temporarily 3) disable continuous batching for that model or tenant 4) bump kvcache_shards or restart batcher workers. Which is fastest?
Dave (runtime): Easiest immediate: toggle per-tenant continuous_batching=false for CUST-5421 via config flag; that will reduce KV churn (each request processed separately), and should drop queue backlog quickly. Also we can add a temporary request limiter rule to cap QPS from that tenant.
Alex (support): I'll ask customer to accept a short maintenance window to flip batching flag. ETA from them: 5–10m.
Priya (sre): Meanwhile I can scale kvcache_shards up to 32 for the node pool and roll out a config patch—should be low-risk but may take ~15m to fully warm. I'll start a canary patch for shard bump on non-critical pool.
Dave (runtime): I'll also add a quick instrument: export per-shard lock_wait histogram to /metrics and set an alert threshold so we catch this earlier.
Alex (support): Customer agreed to the flag flip. Proceeding.
Dave (runtime): Flipped continuous_batching=false for tenant=CUST-5421 (deployment id: flip-20260317-01). Observed immediate drop in continuous_batch_backlog: from 1400 -> 120 within 90s. Request_queue_depth fell from 1024 -> 110 in ~2m.
Priya (sre): Confirmed reduced kvcache lock_waits in logs. No more 504s reported by customer. Marking incident as mitigated.
Marta (pm): Next steps: (1) postmortem to capture root cause + test for hot-shard workloads; (2) consider adaptive shard autoscaling or per-tenant cache isolation; (3) add automatic tenant-level spike protection to prevent single tenant from saturating shared kvcache.
Alex (support): Notified customer: "We've mitigated the issue by temporarily disabling continuous batching for your workload and are rolling a patch to reduce shard contention. We'll follow up with root-cause and timeline for permanent fix."
Priya (sre): I'll open a P1 ticket for infra to evaluate shard autoscaling and add playbook: if backlog > 900 and lock_wait > 50ms -> throttle or disable batching automatically.
Dave (runtime): I'll prepare a small runtime patch that adds backpressure signals from kvcache to the gateway so it can reject early rather than letting the queue pile up. PR draft: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/482 (WIP).
Alex (support): Closing customer-facing escalation, leaving internal follow-ups assigned.
Marta (pm): Adding follow-ups to roadmap for Q2.
Alex (support): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
